findings.evidence: The stream event handler passes delegated arguments through networkToolArgsForObservation before upsert (src/hooks/use-chat-stream.ts:265-267). Conversation hydration sanitizes both fetched chat.tool_call arguments (queries.ts:333-339) and assistant tool_call block.arguments (queries.ts:548); direct conversion test covers both raw input forms (tests/unit/showcase-network-credential-chat.test.ts:21-57). The wrapper catches sanitizer failures and substitutes a safe invalid-recipe row (network-urls.ts:175-188), so ordinary malformed JSON-derived config does not throw from either observation caller.

quality_notes: Stream test exercises exported handleToolEvent and asserts the resulting ToolPart args no longer contain canary secrets; hydration test runs dbMessagesToChatMessages with raw assistant-block and raw tool_call-row arguments. Neither test invokes fetchConversationToolCalls itself, so its raw-row mapping is source-reviewed but not boundary-tested.

Assertions inspect the ToolPart args that the timeline renderer/copy UI consumes, but do not render the actual component or invoke its copy action. Source review confirms ConfigurableToolRow renders/copies entry.args, so no raw alternate display path was found.
Malformed-config non-throw behavior follows the observation helper's catch boundary. The inspected tests do not supply malformed config through stream and hydration callers.
